decisive_items: Serum CA-125 was elevated at 95 U/mL
multiloculated complex pelvic mass with thick septations measuring 24 × 18 cm
a predominantly cystic mass measuring 28.3 × 24.4 × 16.3 cm extending from the pelvis to the upper abdomen
response.rationale: The elevated CA-125, complex multiloculated mass with thick septations, and large size strongly indicate ovarian cystadenocarcinoma. Benign cysts (R2, R3, R4) are contradicted by elevated CA-125; torsion (R10) lacks CA-125 elevation and has different clinical features; other infectious/benign conditions (R9, R8, R11, R7) are unsupported by the mass and CA-125. R6C is a broader malignant category but less specific than R1.

rejected.why: Ovarian torsion does not explain elevated CA-125 or the complex multiloculated mass; torsion typically presents with acute pain and reduced CA-125.
Mucinous cystadenoma is benign; elevated CA-125 and thick septations suggest malignancy, not benign cyst.
Dermoid cyst is benign and typically has different imaging features; elevated CA-125 and large complex mass are inconsistent.
Latent tuberculosis alone does not explain the large adnexal mass or elevated CA-125; vital signs normal and no systemic TB findings.
Endometriosis does not produce a 30 cm multiloculated mass with thick septations and elevated CA-125; the mass is too large and complex.
Tuberculous ovarian cyst is not supported by imaging or CA-125; latent TB is incidental.
Serous cystadenoma is benign; elevated CA-125 and thick septations are more consistent with malignancy.
Pelvic inflammatory disease would not cause a 30 cm complex mass with thick septations and elevated CA-125; tenderness and constipation are nonspecific.
Diverticulitis does not explain the ovarian mass or elevated CA-125; normal vital signs and imaging point away.
